title: Cognitive Control Training with de:)press® as an Add-On to Standard Care for Depression: Effects on Symptom Severity in a Specialized Unit
summary:
Depression is a very common and serious mental illness. Many people receive therapy or medication, but often this is not enough to fully recover. Researchers believe that problems with controlling negative thoughts play an important role in causing depression. That’s why a special training was developed to improve this ability. This training is called aPASAT and is offered as a playful app called de:)press®.
In our study, we want to find out if using this app-based training alongside usual treatment in a specialized depression unit helps reduce symptoms. We will compare 106 patients who receive the training in addition to standard care with those who only get the usual treatment.
The main outcome we measure is how severe the depression is four weeks after the training, using a standard rating scale (HAMD-21). This will help us see if the training provides extra benefit.
conditions: Confirmed diagnosis of unipolar major depression according to ICD-10, single or recurrent episode (F32.0, F32.1, F32.2, F33.0, F33.1, F33.2) as the primary clinical condition.

interventions.name: The intervention group (intention-to-treat, ITT) receives a six-week app-based cognitive control training (CCT) using de:)press® as an add-on to treatment-as-usual (TAU), constituting a blended treatment approach. The control group (CG) receives guideline-based treatment as usual (TAU) following study inclusion and baseline assessment (T0). All assessments are repeated at six weeks (T1) and ten weeks (T2). After study completion, the control group may optionally be offered access to cognitive control training

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Eligible participants are adults with a confirmed diagnosis of unipolar major depression (ICD-10 codes F32.0, F32.1, F32.2, F33.0, F33.1, F33.2) as the primary clinical condition. Requirements include signed informed consent, sufficient German language proficiency, and the ability and experience to use a mobile device for the intervention app.
Exclusion criteria:
Participants are excluded in cases of lacking consent capacity, acute suicidality, severe major depression with psychotic features (F32.3, F33.3), mental disorders due to known physiological causes (F00–F09), schizophrenia spectrum and other psychotic disorders (F20, F22, F23, F25), bipolar and related disorders (F30, F31, F34.0), primary alcohol or substance dependence (F1x.2; exception F17.2), intellectual disabilities (F70–F79), somatic or neurological comorbidities affecting cognitive performance, current use of other cognitive control training (CCT) interventions, legal guardianship or institutionalization, and lack of compliance.
